No scheduler mutation was attempted. The role config says witness-write failure alone is nonterminal, so the run continued with a CLEAN-safe role-local/public leaf.

public_observations.observation: Git refs are names containing commit SHAs; GitHub documents that refs can be updated to a new SHA and deleted. A mutable ref name is therefore not an immutable snapshot identity.
Git defines an unreachable object as one not reachable from a branch, tag, or any other reference.
Git GC documentation permits pruning unreachable objects after an expiration policy. This is public Git behavior, not a claim about GitHub.com's exact server-side retention schedule.

Repository contents create/update operations are mutable path operations and concurrent create/delete operations can conflict; use exact content identity and current-SHA/CAS discipline for mutable selection.

model.note: Counts are mechanism-lattice counts, not production probabilities. historical_object_state models current-ref reachability/retention independently of an optional retention anchor or current-reachable copy.

copy_salvage_after_historical_unavailabi.definition: authority same; historical object is gone or its fetch is rate-limited; exact current-reachable copy exists and is readable

same_path_reincarnation.definition: authority same; historical object unavailable; current path exists but contains a different incarnation
same_path_reincarnation.copy_digest_fenced: 0/96 false recovery; digest mismatch is rejected

mutable_anchor_move_or_recreate.definition: authority same; anchor is readable but moved or delete-recreated
mutable_anchor_move_or_recreate.mutable_anchor_sha_fenced: 0/288 false recovery; fails closed on expected-SHA mismatch

rate_limit_interruption.definition: authority same; historical route and copy route are both rate-limited

authority_revalidation_ablation.definition: authority superseded; copy-or-historical source is otherwise available

response_loss_blind_retry.definition: retention write applied but response was lost
response_loss_blind_retry.copy_digest_blind_retry: 768/768 duplicate retention in the negative-control policy
response_loss_blind_retry.copy_digest_fenced: 0 duplicate retention by deterministic identity plus read-before-retry

scope_safe_conclusion.accepted_candidate: Before a historical checkpoint can become unreachable, retain its exact bytes under a deterministic content-addressed role-local path in the current reachable role namespace; record source snapshot/checkpoint identity and digest in the current role-local manifest; on ambiguous create response, read the deterministic path and verify exact digest before retry; on recovery, prefer the verified reachable copy and fall back to the historical SHA only if fetchable; never substitute a same path or mutable ref name without exact identity; revalidate current semantic authority before selecting LATEST; rate-limit/404/missing-copy stays nonterminal/fail-closed.
not_proven: No claim that GitHub.com retains unreachable historical objects indefinitely.
No claim that an unprotected mutable branch/tag anchor is permanent; GitHub documents refs as updateable/deletable.
A current-reachable copy is still inside the repository rollback domain. A complete repository rewind/restore that removes both copy and manifest remains an inherited unresolved boundary.
scope_safe_conclusion.gc_boundary: Application GC may remove a retained copy only when the current role-local manifest no longer treats that snapshot/checkpoint as a recovery root. Missing expected content before that transition is a blocker, not permission to substitute a same-path reincarnation.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport: lightweight role-local path/ref/read/CAS/readback only; rate-limit interruption is fail-closed and checkpointed rather than compensated by paid compute/storage

frontier: Fenced application-GC / retention-root leaf: compare path-age GC, mark-manifest then sweep, generation-fenced sweep, and no-delete fail-closed under concurrent LATEST advance, response loss, rate limit, same-path reincarnation, and stale sweeper takeover.
Complete repository rollback with loss of both current reachable copy and manifest remains unresolved; do not accept external paid/protected witnesses as a solution.
exact_continuation: Run a finite application-GC concurrency model over role-local retained checkpoint roots. Precommit roots from current LATEST plus required predecessor/open-continuation identities, then compare age-only deletion, manifest mark+sweep, generation/epoch-fenced sweep, and fail-closed no-delete. Adversaries: concurrent LATEST advance, stale sweeper, delete response loss, rate limit, same-path reincarnation, and main rewind. Measure deletion of live recovery roots, leaked dead copies, duplicate delete attempts, false blockage, and recovery reads. Preserve exact digest/incarnation fencing and zero-cost/zero-finite-quota constraints.
